title: Copperridge Client — integration lifecycle notes (internal)
body:
Context / why this exists:
- Copperridge (claims operations co.) evaluating Private deployment in their Azure VNet.  Sensitive PII, must satisfy regional data residency and HSM-backed keying.
- Initial ask: replace legacy rules engine with LLM-powered claim summarizer + classification. They expect bursty traffic tied to business hours (08:00-18:00 ET).

Call snapshot (2025-01-24) — attendees:
- Copperridge: Dana Morales (Head of Ops), Elias Chen (Platform), Rajiv Nair (Security)
- Redwood: Avery Chen (SE), Marco Ruiz (Infra SE), Leah Goldberg (SRE liaison)

High-level goals from customer:
- Keep all raw PII in-country (US-only region) and prevent model telemetry leaving tenant VNet.
- <1s token latency target for short summaries (avg 80–120 tokens).
- 99.9% availability during business hours, graceful degradation off-hours.
- Ability to roll back to deterministic rules for high-risk claims.

Quick technical constraints noted:
- Copperridge uses Azure Gov? (they said a compliant tenant; Rajiv to confirm exact tenancy). This affects our AMI/container images and region selection.
- They require KMS integration: HSM-backed keys for model prompt storage and for encrypting cache seeds.
- Firewall policy: outbound egress only to a small allowlist; cannot dial out to public internet except to approved Redwood endpoints via private link.
- Audit/logging retention: 2 years for request/response metadata (not raw text). Must reconcile with our standard retention.
- On-prem footprint: initially VPC-hosted private control plane, but may want fully air-gapped later.

Serving profile & model choices (initial proposal) — notes to self:
- Start with a mid-size Llama-derivative (13B FP16/8-bit-LLM) tuned for summarization. Rationale: balance latency vs cost; their summary length small so smaller context window ok.
- Enable KV caching for intra-session multi-turn claim triage (expected repeated lookups per claim). Configure TTL conservatively (2–4 hours) to avoid stale state.
- Quantization path: ship 8-bit with per-channel quant kernels where available; fall back to FP16 on failover nodes. Document perf delta.
- Consider serving a distilled 7B variant as fallback for capacity constraints to meet latency SLO — must measure delta in hallucination rate on our eval set.

Performance assumptions & KPIs to validate:
- Baseline perf target: 0.7–1.2s p50 for 100-token outputs at 1.5k concurrent sessions during business hours.
- Throughput expected: 40–60 QPS sustained with bursts to 150 QPS for 10–15 minutes.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement flagged $/k token impact; recommend dedicated pool to control unit costs.

Network & security gotchas (explicit):
- PrivateLink setup will require IP allowlist + cert pinning for our control-plane to agent communications. Need SRE template.
- Azure NSGs often block ephemeral ports used by our inter-node KV sync; include coordinator in infra runbook.
- HSM keywrap: our current KMS integration assumes GCP/AWS HSM APIs. Confirm Azure KeyVault HSM parity (Rajiv to confirm API model).
- Logging redaction: they want tokens redacted from stored payloads. We currently keep request hashes + truncated tokens for debugging — verify retention & redaction capability with legal.

Rollout / canary plan (practical draft):
1) Sandbox deploy in a Copperridge dev VNet with synthetic traffic (perf target validation).
2) Staged sync to preprod VNet; connect their SRE to tail logs and SLO dashboard.
3) Canary group = 5% of claims traffic (sampling via their gateway header). Monitor: latency, error-rate, hallucination-rate on prompt set. 48-hour window.
4) 25% increment after 24–48h if thresholds ok; automatic rollback if 5xxs > 0.5% or latency p95 > 2.5s.

Preflight checklist (items to complete before prod cut):
- [ ] Confirm Azure tenancy and subscription IDs (Elias)
- [ ] KMS/HSM proof-of-parity doc (Marco)
- [ ] PrivateLink endpoint names & IPs (Copperridge network)
- [ ] Data residency & logging redaction policy sign-off from legal (Dana + Redwood legal)
- [ ] Baseline eval: hallucination/regression test using Copperridge sample prompts (Leah)
- [ ] Dedicated capacity sizing proposal + pricing (Avery + Billing)
- [ ] Incident runbook with rollback steps to rules engine (steps documented & tested)

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Marco: spin a dev node in our Azure sandbox and test KeyVault HSM wrapping (due 2025-01-30).
- Leah: create a small eval harness with 600 Copperridge-like claim samples and run 3 model variants (13B FP16, 8-bit 13B, distilled 7B) — capture accuracy + hallucination metrics (due 2025-01-29).
- I (Avery): draft the private-link SRE template and a short security Q&A for Rajiv (due 2025-01-28).
- Dana: send exact compliance doc + retention policy; confirm if healthcare PHI rules apply (due 2025-01-31).

Open questions / risks (for sales & product):
- Price sensitivity: will Copperridge sign up for a reserved dedicated pool vs pay-as-you-go? We need to map unit economics for both.
- Air-gapped option: if they request air-gapped, our support cost increases substantially. Estimate required (ops FTE) before they commit.
- Latency window viability: their <1s target might be optimistic for certain worst-case claim narratives; need to surface that as a scope item.

Notes-to-self (fragile, informal):
- Watch out for repeated ask: "no telemetry leaves our VNet" — implies we may need to run everything (including evaluation harness) in their VNet for true compliance. Push back where possible but prepare plan.
- If they force HSM-wrapped cache keys, we need to ensure cache node affinity to region to avoid decryption hops.
- Keep canary small. Their ops team is nervous and will call rollback at first hiccup.

Meeting artifacts to attach when sending recap:
- Link to eval harness (Leah's folder)
- Perf run screenshots + simple perf table (p50/p95)
- Proposed contract terms: reserved pool vs monthly (high level numbers)
- Runbook draft for rollback to rules engine

Who owns follow-ups:
- Overall: Avery (SE) — own coordination + pricing proposal
- Infra proofs: Marco
- Eval & quality: Leah
- Copperridge legal/compliance liaisons: Dana / Rajiv

End notes (tone: pragmatic). This will be a multi-sprint onboarding. Primary trust blockers are: KMS parity, network posture (PrivateLink/NSG), and a clean story for audit/redaction. If we get the eval numbers within 2 weeks and infra proofs, sales can move to a reserved-capacity proposal.

Random fragments captured mid-call (raw):
- "We can’t have inference logs for 24 months" — Dana (probably meaning metadata only)
- "If a claim is flagged high-risk, auto-fallback to rules, but still show AI suggestion in UI"
- Rajiv: "We need a paper trail for every decision; what metadata do you ship?" -> need mapping table

-- Avery C.
(putting this here to stop overwriting notes in Slack)
